question: Aid or auxiliary to trade includes which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Warehousing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aids (or auxiliaries) to trade are the services that facilitate the smooth movement of goods from producers to consumers — they support trade but are not trade itself. (व्यापार के सहायक — भंडारण)

 

• The main aids to trade include transportation, warehousing, banking, insurance, advertising and communication.

 

• Warehousing refers to the storage of goods until they are needed, bridging the gap between production and consumption — it is a classic auxiliary/aid to trade.

 

• Production, buying and selling are core commercial/industrial activities themselves, not aids that support trade.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Trade itself is broadly classified into home trade (wholesale and retail) and foreign trade (import, export and entrepot).

 

• Other auxiliaries to trade such as banking (provides finance) and insurance (covers risk) are equally essential for the smooth conduct of trade.

 

NOTE

 

• Production (Option 1): This is an industrial activity that creates goods; it precedes trade and is not itself an aid to trade.

 

• Selling (Option 2): This is one of the two components of trade (buying and selling), not an auxiliary to it.

 

• Buying (Option 3): Like selling, buying is a part of trade itself, not a service that assists trade.

question: Nrityabharati Kathak Dance Academy in Pune was established by which of the following Sangeet Natak Akademi Awardees?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rohini Bhate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rohini Bhate was an eminent Kathak dancer, choreographer and guru from Pune, Maharashtra. (नृत्यभारती कथक नृत्य अकादमी — रोहिणी भाटे)

 

• She founded the Nrityabharati Kathak Dance Academy in Pune to train students in the Kathak tradition.

 

• She was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Kathak, and later with the Padma Shri for her contribution to Indian classical dance.

 

• She is remembered for blending traditional Kathak technique with new choreographic experiments and for her scholarly writing on dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, traditionally associated with North India and known for its intricate footwork, spins (chakkars) and storytelling (abhinaya).

 

• Other well-known Kathak exponents include Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi and Kumudini Lakhia.

 

NOTE

 

• Roshan Kumari (Option 2): A renowned Kathak dancer of the Jaipur gharana, but she did not found this academy.

 

• Kumidini Lakhia (Option 3): A celebrated Kathak dancer and founder of the Kadamb Centre for Dance in Ahmedabad, not the Pune academy.

 

• Sitara Devi (Option 4): A legendary Kathak dancer of the Banaras gharana, known as "Nritya Samragini", but not the founder of this Pune academy.

question: The Government of ______ launched Mukhyamantri Chaa Srami Kalyan Prakalpa Scheme for tea garden workers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tripura.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of Tripura launched the "Mukhyamantri Chaa Srami Kalyan Prakalpa" scheme in March 2022 for the welfare of tea garden workers in the state. (चाय श्रमिक कल्याण प्रकल्प — त्रिपुरा)

 

• The scheme aims to provide social security benefits — including financial assistance for housing, health and other welfare measures — to workers employed in Tripura's tea gardens.

 

• It was announced by the then Chief Minister of Tripura, Biplab Kumar Deb.

 

• Tripura has a significant tea-growing belt, and tea garden labourers form an important workforce segment, making such welfare schemes economically and socially significant for the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tripura is known for its tea gardens, particularly in areas around Kamalpur and other northern districts of the state.

 

• Other states with major tea industries and worker-welfare schemes include Assam and West Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Not the state associated with this scheme; Kerala's tea industry is concentrated in the Western Ghats (e.g., Munnar).

 

• Assam (Option 2): India's largest tea-producing state, but this particular scheme was launched by Tripura, not Assam.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Not a major tea-producing state and not linked to this scheme.

question: The world’s longest river the Nile flows through which of the following continent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Africa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nile River, widely regarded as the longest river in the world (about 6,650 km), flows through north-eastern Africa. (नील नदी — अफ्रीका)

 

• It flows through several African countries including Uganda, Sudan, South Sudan and Egypt, before draining into the Mediterranean Sea.

 

• Its two major tributaries are the White Nile (originating from Lake Victoria region) and the Blue Nile (originating from Lake Tana, Ethiopia), which meet at Khartoum, Sudan.

 

• The Nile has been central to the civilisation of ancient Egypt, providing water and fertile silt for agriculture in an otherwise arid region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Amazon River in South America is the largest river by discharge volume and is sometimes cited as rivaling the Nile in length in some recent studies.

 

• The famous Aswan High Dam is built on the Nile in Egypt.

 

NOTE

 

• North America (Option 2): Major rivers here include the Mississippi and Missouri, not the Nile.

 

• South America (Option 3): Home to the Amazon River, not the Nile.

 

• Europe (Option 4): Major rivers here include the Volga and Danube, not the Nile.

question: Taking cognizance of the pandemic situation in 2021, the Ministry of Ayush, GoI decided the message of International Day of Yoga 2021 celebration will be:
option_2: Be with Yoga, Be at Home!
option_3: Yoga at Home, Yoga with Family!
solution_text:
The correct answer is Be with Yoga, Be at Home!.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 7th International Day of Yoga (21 June 2021) was observed under the theme/message "Be with Yoga, Be at Home!". (योग दिवस 2021 — बी विद योगा, बी एट होम)

 

• Considering the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, encouraged citizens to practise yoga at home with family, rather than at large public gatherings.

 

• International Day of Yoga is observed every year on 21 June, following a proposal by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the UN General Assembly in 2014.

 

• The theme reflected the need to maintain physical and mental well-being through yoga while adhering to safety protocols during the pandemic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The theme for International Day of Yoga 2022 was "Yoga for Humanity", and for 2023 it was "Yoga for Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" (Yoga for One World, One Health).

 

• The idea of International Day of Yoga was first proposed at the UN General Assembly on 27 September 2014.

 

NOTE

 

• Yoga at Home (Option 1): Not the officially adopted message for 2021; the actual phrase used was more specific.

 

• Yoga at Home, Yoga with Family! (Option 3): This was actually the message for International Day of Yoga 2020, not 2021.

 

• Home Yoga and Yoga Home (Option 4): Not an official theme/message used by the Ministry of Ayush.

question: Which of the following is NOT a capital expenditure?
option_1: Loans and advances by the central government
option_2: Expenditure on the acquisition of land
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subsidies payment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Capital expenditure refers to spending that either creates an asset or reduces a liability — for example, buying land/buildings, making investments, or giving loans. Subsidies, by contrast, are a revenue expenditure. (पूंजीगत व्यय बनाम राजस्व व्यय — सब्सिडी राजस्व व्यय है)

 

• Subsidies are recurring payments made by the government to reduce the cost of goods/services for consumers or producers (e.g., food, fertilizer, fuel subsidies); they neither create an asset nor reduce a liability, so they are classified under revenue expenditure.

 

• Loans and advances by the central government (Option 1) create a financial asset (a claim/receivable) for the government, hence they are capital expenditure.

 

• Acquisition of land (Option 2) and investment in shares (Option 3) both directly create physical or financial assets for the government, and are therefore capital expenditure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Union Budget in India is divided into the Revenue Budget (revenue receipts and revenue expenditure) and the Capital Budget (capital receipts and capital expenditure).

 

• Other examples of revenue expenditure include salaries, pensions, interest payments, and grants-in-aid.

 

NOTE

 

• Loans and advances by the central government (Option 1): This is capital expenditure since it creates a financial asset for the government.

 

• Expenditure on the acquisition of land (Option 2): This creates a physical/fixed asset, making it capital expenditure.

 

• Investment in shares (Option 3): This creates a financial asset, making it capital expenditure.

question: Padma Shri awardee, Gulabo Sapera is a _________ dancer of Rajasthan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbelia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gulabo Sapera is a renowned Kalbelia dancer from Rajasthan, credited with popularising this folk dance form nationally and internationally. (कालबेलिया नृत्य — गुलाबो सपेरा)

 

• Kalbelia dance is performed by the Kalbelia (Sapera/snake-charmer) community of Rajasthan; dancers wear black swirling skirts and move in snake-like, sinuous movements.

 

• Gulabo Sapera was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2016 for her contribution to Kalbelia folk dance.

 

• Kalbelia dance was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Rajasthan include Ghoomar (performed by women, especially of the Bhil community), Bhavai (balancing pots on the head), and Terah Taali (performed by Kamad community women using manjeeras/cymbals tied to the body).

 

• Kalbelia songs and dances draw on stories from Rajasthani folklore, including tales of the snake-charmer community.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhavai (Option 1): A Rajasthani folk dance involving balancing multiple pots/pitchers on the head, not Gulabo Sapera's dance form.

 

• Terah Taali (Option 2): A ritual dance performed by women of the Kamad community using cymbals, unrelated to Gulabo Sapera.

 

• Ghoomar (Option 4): A traditional community dance of Rajasthan performed by women in swirling ghagras, distinct from Kalbelia.

question: The region of Ganga Brahmaputra basin lies in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10°N to 30°N latitude.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ganga-Brahmaputra river basin — the largest river basin in India — lies approximately between 10°N and 30°N latitude. (गंगा-ब्रह्मपुत्र बेसिन — 10° उ. से 30° उ. अक्षांश)

 

• This basin covers a vast area across North, Central and Eastern India, as well as parts of Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan and China, and is one of the most fertile and densely populated river basins in the world.

 

• The Ganga originates from the Gangotri glacier in the Himalayas, while the Brahmaputra originates near Mansarovar Lake in Tibet and enters India through Arunachal Pradesh.

 

• The combined basin drains into the Bay of Bengal through the world's largest delta, the Sunderbans.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ganga basin alone covers roughly 26% of India's total land area, making it the largest river basin in the country.

 

• The Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system together forms one of the largest freshwater deltas in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• 10°N to 10°N latitude (Option 1): This is not a valid latitude range (same value given twice) and does not represent the basin's extent.

 

• 30°N to 50°N latitude (Option 2): This range lies too far north and does not correspond to the Indian subcontinent's Ganga-Brahmaputra region.

 

• 5°N to 10°N latitude (Option 3): This range is too far south, closer to equatorial regions, and does not match the basin's actual location.

question: Which state government launched the Matrushakti Udaymita Scheme to provide support to women entrepreneurs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of Haryana launched the "Mukhyamantri Matrushakti Udyamita Yojana" to promote and support women entrepreneurs in the state. (मातृशक्ति उद्यमिता योजना — हरियाणा)

 

• The scheme aims to provide financial and institutional support, including easier access to loans and subsidies, to encourage women to set up and run their own businesses/micro-enterprises.

 

• It falls under Haryana's broader efforts toward women's economic empowerment and self-reliance (aligned with initiatives like Atmanirbhar Bharat).

 

• The scheme is implemented through the Haryana Women Development Corporation to reach eligible women across the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other states have similar women-entrepreneurship schemes, such as Rajasthan's various self-help-group linked schemes and Madhya Pradesh's entrepreneurship promotion policies.

 

• Haryana has also launched several other welfare schemes such as Beti Bachao Beti Padhao support measures and skill-development programmes for women.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Not the state associated with the Matrushakti Udyamita Scheme.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 2): Runs its own set of women-entrepreneurship schemes but did not launch this particular scheme.

 

• Gujarat (Option 4): Known for schemes like Mission Mangalam for women's self-help groups, but not this specific scheme.

question: Which of the following revolutionaries stated during his trial that “he did not wish to glorify the cult of the bomb and pistol but wanted a revolution in society”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhagat Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhagat Singh, during his trial following the Central Legislative Assembly bombing (1929) and the Lahore Conspiracy Case, clarified that he did not want to "glorify the cult of the bomb and pistol" but sought a revolution in society based on justice and equality. (भगत सिंह — बम और पिस्तौल का पंथ नहीं, समाज में क्रांति)

 

• He, along with Batukeshwar Dutt, threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929 to protest repressive laws, deliberately avoiding casualties, and then courted arrest to use the trial as a platform to spread revolutionary ideas.

 

• Bhagat Singh's writings and courtroom statements emphasised socialism, secularism and the need for a just social order, distinguishing his ideology from mere terrorism.

 

• He was a founding member of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) and was executed on 23 March 1931 along with Rajguru and Sukhdev.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhagat Singh's famous slogan was "Inquilab Zindabad" (Long Live the Revolution).

 

• His key ideological essay, "Why I am an Atheist", was written while he was in jail awaiting execution.

 

NOTE

 

• Surya Sen (Option 2): Led the Chittagong Armoury Raid (1930); this particular trial statement is not attributed to him.

 

• Sachindra Nath Sanyal (Option 3): A founder of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), associated with the Kakori Conspiracy, but not the source of this statement.

 

• Barindra Kumar Ghosh (Option 4): Associated with the Alipore Bomb Case and early revolutionary activities in Bengal, but this statement is not attributed to him.

question: Abhinav Bharat Society was a secret society of revolutionaries. It was established in __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay Presidency.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Abhinav Bharat Society was a secret revolutionary organisation founded in 1904 by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar in Nashik, which was part of the Bombay Presidency. (अभिनव भारत सोसाइटी — बॉम्बे प्रेसीडेंसी)

 

• The society aimed to organise armed resistance against British colonial rule and inspire revolutionary nationalism among the youth.

 

• Members of the society were linked to acts such as the assassination of A.M.T. Jackson, the District Magistrate of Nashik, in 1909.

 

• The organisation later merged with the Free India Society established by Savarkar in London, extending its revolutionary network abroad.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bombay Presidency was also home to other nationalist activities and was a key centre for the Ganapati and Shivaji festivals started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

 

• Other contemporary revolutionary groups included Anushilan Samiti (Bengal) and Ghadar Party (Punjab/USA).

 

NOTE

 

• United Provinces (Option 2): Associated with revolutionary activity such as the Kakori Conspiracy, but not the founding location of Abhinav Bharat.

 

• Punjab Province (Option 3): Home to organisations like the Ghadar Party, not Abhinav Bharat Society.

 

• Calcutta Presidency (Option 4): Bengal (Calcutta) was the base of Anushilan Samiti and Jugantar, not Abhinav Bharat, which was founded in Bombay Presidency.

question: The British physicist named Paul Dirac was known to have introduced the concept of _________ in 1930.
solution_text:
The correct answer is antiparticle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Paul Dirac, a British theoretical physicist, formulated the Dirac equation in 1928, which combined quantum mechanics with special relativity, and in 1930-31 predicted the existence of the antiparticle (an oppositely charged "mirror" particle for every particle, such as the positron for the electron). (पॉल डिराक — प्रतिकण/एंटीपार्टिकल)

 

• His prediction of the positron (the antiparticle of the electron) was experimentally confirmed by Carl D. Anderson in 1932.

 

• For this work, Dirac shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Erwin Schrödinger "for the discovery of new productive forms of atomic theory".

 

• The concept of antiparticles laid the foundation for the field of antimatter physics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Dirac equation remains fundamental to quantum field theory and predicts the existence of antimatter as a natural consequence of combining quantum mechanics with relativity.

 

• Other key contributors to atomic and particle physics include Niels Bohr (atomic model) and Ernest Rutherford (nuclear model of atom).

 

NOTE

 

• thermal ionisation (Option 1): Associated with the work of physicist Meghnad Saha (Saha ionisation equation), not Dirac.

 

• cosmic radiation (Option 2): Cosmic rays were discovered by Victor Hess in 1912, unrelated to Dirac's 1930 work.

 

• nuclear model of atom (Option 3): Proposed by Ernest Rutherford in 1911, not by Dirac in 1930.

question: Which of the following was awarded to Bharatnatyam dancer, Priyadarshini Govind in 1998?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalaimamani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Priyadarshini Govind is an acclaimed Bharatanatyam dancer known for her mastery of abhinaya (expressive storytelling).

 

• She was awarded the Kalaimamani title by the Government of Tamil Nadu in 1998, in recognition of her contribution to classical dance. (कलैमामणि — प्रियदर्शिनी गोविंद, 1998)

 

• She later received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (2012) and the Nritya Choodamani title from Sri Krishna Gana Sabha (2015) for her continued excellence in Bharatanatyam.

 

• She has also served as a director of Kalakshetra Foundation, Chennai, a premier institution for classical dance and music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kalaimamani is a state honour conferred annually by the Tamil Nadu Government's Department of Art and Culture on eminent artists.

 

• Priyadarshini Govind has performed and taught Bharatanatyam extensively across India and internationally.

 

NOTE

 

• Tagore Ratna (Option 1): Not an award received by Priyadarshini Govind in 1998.

 

• Nritya Choodamani (Option 3): This was awarded to her later, in 2015, not in 1998.

 

• Kalidas Samman (Option 4): A prestigious award given by the Madhya Pradesh government to artists, but not the one Priyadarshini Govind received in 1998.

question: Which special order of the courts means “arrested person should be presented before the court”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Habeas corpus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Habeas corpus is a Latin term meaning "you must have the body", and it is a writ that directs a detaining authority to produce the arrested/detained person before the court. (हैबियस कॉर्पस — बंदी प्रत्यक्षीकरण)

 

• This writ is used to safeguard individual liberty against unlawful detention, ensuring that no person is held without legal justification.

 

• Under the Constitution of India, the power to issue this and other writs lies with the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the High Courts (Article 226).

 

• If the detention is found to be illegal, the court orders the immediate release of the person.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's writ jurisdiction is inspired by English common law, and includes five types of writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto.

 

• Mandamus means "we command" and is issued to a public authority to perform its official duty.

 

NOTE

 

• Mandamus (Option 2): A writ commanding a public official/body to perform a duty it is obligated to perform; unrelated to producing a detained person.

 

• Certiorari (Option 3): Issued by a higher court to quash the order of a lower court/tribunal that has exceeded its jurisdiction.

 

• Quo warranto (Option 4): Issued to question the legal authority/right of a person holding a public office.

question: A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed only on the grounds of _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is proven misbehaviour or incapacity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 124(4) of the Constitution of India, a judge of the Supreme Court can be removed only on the grounds of "proved misbehaviour or incapacity". (न्यायाधीश को हटाना — सिद्ध कदाचार या अक्षमता)

 

• The removal process (called impeachment) requires a motion supported by a special majority in both Houses of Parliament in the same session, followed by presentation of an address to the President.

 

• This provision ensures the independence of the judiciary by making the removal process deliberately rigorous and insulated from ordinary political pressure.

 

• The same grounds and broadly similar procedure apply to the removal of High Court judges as well, under Article 217/218 read with Article 124.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 lays down the detailed procedure for investigating charges of misbehaviour or incapacity against a judge before a removal motion can proceed.

 

• To date, no Supreme Court or High Court judge in India has ever been successfully removed through this impeachment process.

 

NOTE

 

• Disrespect of the Constitution (Option 1): Not a specifically named constitutional ground for removal of a judge.

 

• Murder charges (Option 3): Criminal charges would be dealt with separately under ordinary law, not as the constitutional ground for judicial removal.

 

• Lack of knowledge (Option 4): Not a constitutionally recognised ground for removing a judge.

question: Which of the following has discovered the sea route to India 1498?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vasco Da Gama.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vasco da Gama, a Portuguese explorer, discovered the sea route to India in 1498, sailing around the Cape of Good Hope to land at Calicut (Kozhikode), Kerala. (वास्को डी गामा — भारत के लिए समुद्री मार्ग, 1498)

 

• His voyage opened direct maritime trade links between Europe and India, bypassing the overland routes controlled by Ottoman and Arab intermediaries.

 

• He landed at Calicut, then ruled by the Zamorin, and this event marked the beginning of the era of European colonial expansion in India.

 

• Vasco da Gama later served as the Portuguese Viceroy of India and died in Kochi in 1524 during his third voyage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Cape of Good Hope route was first rounded by Bartolomeu Dias in 1488, paving the way for da Gama's later voyage to India.

 

• The arrival of Vasco da Gama eventually led to the establishment of Portuguese colonies in India, including Goa, which became a major Portuguese base.

 

NOTE

 

• Clive Lord (Option 1): Not a historical figure associated with the discovery of the sea route to India.

 

• Henry the sailor (Option 2): Likely refers to Prince Henry the Navigator of Portugal, who sponsored early voyages of exploration but did not himself sail to India.

 

• Captain Hudson (Option 3): Refers to Henry Hudson, an English explorer known for voyages in North America, unrelated to the sea route to India.

question: Which of the following is the first ‘smoke-free state’ in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Himachal Pradesh became India's first "smoke-free state", having achieved this status through strict enforcement of anti-smoking laws banning smoking in public places. (धूम्रपान मुक्त राज्य — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

 

• The state implemented the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), 2003 rigorously, prohibiting smoking in public places such as bus stands, offices, hospitals and educational institutions.

 

• Himachal Pradesh has also been recognised for its National Tobacco Control Programme performance, being adjudged among the best-performing states.

 

• This achievement is often cited in the context of public health initiatives and tobacco-control policy in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India ratified the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) in 2004, which has guided many state-level anti-tobacco measures.

 

• Other states have since undertaken similar smoke-free initiatives, but Himachal Pradesh was the pioneer.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan (Option 1): Not recognised as India's first smoke-free state.

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 2): Has undertaken tobacco-control measures but is not the first smoke-free state.

 

• Bihar (Option 3): Not associated with being India's first smoke-free state.

question: What is the distance of the penalty mark from the midpoint of the goal post in football?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11 m.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In football (soccer), the penalty mark (penalty spot) is placed 11 metres (12 yards) from the midpoint of the goal line, directly in front of the goal. (पेनल्टी स्पॉट — गोल से 11 मीटर)

 

• This distance is fixed as part of the Laws of the Game, maintained by the International Football Association Board (IFAB), which governs standard football pitch and equipment dimensions.

 

• The penalty area (18-yard box) measures 40.3 m x 16.5 m, and the penalty mark sits centrally within it, 11 m from goal.

 

• A penalty kick is awarded when a direct free-kick offence is committed by the defending team inside its own penalty area.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The standard football goal measures 7.32 m (8 yards) wide and 2.44 m (8 feet) high.

 

• The penalty arc, drawn 9.15 m from the penalty mark, ensures other players stay clear during a penalty kick.

 

NOTE

 

• 10 m (Option 1): Not the standard penalty spot distance as per FIFA/IFAB rules.

 

• 15 m (Option 2): Too far from the goal; not the correct penalty mark distance.

 

• 13 m (Option 4): Also not the correct measurement; the standard is fixed at 11 m.

question: Which of the following type of house remains were found in Mehrgarh site of Harappan civilization?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Square or rectangular.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mehrgarh, located in present-day Balochistan, Pakistan, is one of the earliest known farming settlements (Neolithic period, c. 7000 BCE) and a precursor to the mature Harappan (Indus Valley) civilization. (मेहरगढ़ — वर्गाकार/आयताकार मकान)

 

• Excavations at Mehrgarh revealed the remains of square or rectangular houses, typically built of mud-bricks, some of which had multiple internal compartments believed to be used for storage.

 

• The site provides crucial evidence of the transition from a hunter-gatherer to a settled agricultural lifestyle, including early domestication of plants (wheat, barley) and animals (cattle, sheep, goats).

 

• Mehrgarh is regarded as a key site for understanding the origins of the Indus Valley Civilization, showing continuous cultural development over several millennia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mehrgarh was discovered in 1974 by a French archaeological team led by Jean-François Jarrige.

 

• The site's occupation spans roughly from 7000 BCE to 2600 BCE, just before the emergence of mature Harappan urban centres like Mohenjodaro and Harappa.

 

NOTE

 

• Triangular or circular (Option 1): Not the house shapes documented at Mehrgarh.

 

• Rectangular or circular (Option 2): Mixes the correct rectangular shape with an incorrect circular shape; circular houses are not the documented type at Mehrgarh.

 

• Circular or square (Option 4): Similarly mixes an incorrect circular shape with the correct square shape.

question: In 1893, which Swiss chemist was the first to understand the molecular structures of inorganic substances – chemical compounds that do not contain carbon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alfred Werner.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alfred Werner, a Swiss chemist, proposed his coordination theory in 1893, explaining the molecular structure of inorganic coordination compounds (compounds without carbon-based/organic backbones). (आल्फ्रेड वर्नर — समन्वय सिद्धांत, 1893)

 

• His theory introduced concepts such as primary and secondary valency, laying the foundation for modern coordination chemistry.

 

• For this pioneering work, Werner was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1913 — becoming the first inorganic chemist to receive this honour.

 

• His work helped explain the geometry and bonding of complex metal-ligand compounds, which are central to modern inorganic and bioinorganic chemistry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• John Dalton is known for his atomic theory (early 19th century), unrelated to coordination chemistry.

 

• William Ramsay discovered several noble gases (helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon) and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1904.

 

NOTE

 

• William Ramsay (Option 2): Known for discovering noble gases, not for coordination chemistry.

 

• George de Hevesy (Option 3): Known for pioneering work on radioactive tracers and co-discovery of the element hafnium, not coordination theory.

 

• John Dalton (Option 4): Known for the atomic theory of matter, proposed much earlier (early 1800s), unrelated to 1893 coordination chemistry.

question: ______ gas is used for the manufacturing of bleaching powder.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chlorine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bleaching powder (calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂) is manufactured by passing chlorine gas over dry slaked lime (calcium hydroxide). (ब्लीचिंग पाउडर — क्लोरीन गैस)

 

• The reaction is: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O, producing bleaching powder used for disinfection, water purification and as a bleaching agent in the textile and paper industries.

 

• This process is also known as the Backmann process for industrial-scale bleaching powder production.

 

• Chlorine is a strong oxidising agent, which gives bleaching powder its characteristic bleaching and disinfecting properties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chlorine gas is also used in the manufacture of PVC (polyvinyl chloride) and for the disinfection of drinking water.

 

• Bleaching powder gradually releases chlorine on exposure to air/moisture, which is responsible for its characteristic pungent smell.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrogen (Option 1): An inert gas used mainly in fertilizers and as an inert atmosphere; not used to make bleaching powder.

 

• Sulphur (Option 2): Used in the manufacture of sulphuric acid and other sulphur compounds, not bleaching powder.

 

• Oxygen (Option 3): Essential for combustion and respiration, but not the gas used to manufacture bleaching powder.

question: Which of the following dance forms is associated with the state of Himachal Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dhaman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dhaman is a traditional folk dance of Himachal Pradesh, performed by local communities during festivals and social gatherings. (धमन नृत्य — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

 

• Himachal Pradesh has a rich repertoire of folk dances including Nati, Kinnauri, Thoda, Jhora, Jhali, Chharhi, Chhapeli, Mahasu and Dhaman, each associated with particular regions or communities of the state.

 

• These dances are typically performed during local fairs and festivals such as Kullu Dussehra and other regional harvest and religious celebrations.

 

• Nati, another Himachali dance, holds a Guinness World Record for the largest folk dance performance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Himachal Pradesh's folk culture reflects its diverse ethnic groups, including the Kinnauras, Gaddis and Kullu valley communities.

 

• Folk dances often use traditional instruments like the shehnai, dhol and narsingha.

 

NOTE

 

• Rauf (Option 1): A traditional folk dance of Kashmir, performed mainly by women, not Himachal Pradesh.

 

• Phagua (Option 3): A folk dance associated with the Holi festival in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, not Himachal Pradesh.

 

• Koli (Option 4): A folk dance of the fishing communities of coastal Maharashtra and Goa, not Himachal Pradesh.

question: In which of the following groups, are all plants monoecious?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maize, Cucumber, Fig and Melon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Monoecious plants bear both male and female reproductive structures (unisexual flowers of both sexes) on the same individual plant. (एकलिंगाश्रयी पादप — मक्का, ककड़ी, अंजीर, खरबूजा)

 

• Maize (corn) bears separate male flowers (tassel) and female flowers (cob) on the same plant — a classic example of a monoecious plant.

 

• Cucumber and Melon (Cucurbitaceae family) typically bear separate male and female flowers on the same vine, making them monoecious.

 

• Fig (Ficus) is generally treated as monoecious in this classification, bearing both types of flowers within its unique syconium (fig fruit-like structure) on the same plant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Papaya and Poplar are classic examples of dioecious plants, where separate male and female individuals exist (i.e., a single plant bears only male or only female flowers).

 

• Rose plants are typically bisexual/hermaphroditic (each flower has both stamens and pistils), which is a different classification from monoecious/dioecious.

 

NOTE

 

• Maize, Papaya, Poplar and Rose (Option 1): Incorrect because Papaya and Poplar are dioecious, not monoecious.

 

• Papaya, Poplar, Rose and Fig (Option 2): Incorrect because Papaya and Poplar are dioecious.

 

• Cucumber, Papaya, Poplar and Rose (Option 4): Incorrect because Papaya and Poplar are dioecious.

question: The annual growth rate percentage population in India gradually started declining in the year ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1981.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's annual population growth rate began gradually declining after 1981, marking a shift in the country's demographic transition. (जनसंख्या वृद्धि दर में गिरावट — 1981 से)

 

• The decadal growth rate had peaked around 1961-1981, and from the 1981-1991 decade onward, the growth rate started showing a gradual decline, attributed to falling fertility rates and improved family planning/health outcomes.

 

• This decline reflects India's progress through the stages of the demographic transition model, moving from high birth/death rates toward more moderate rates.

 

• Factors contributing to the decline include increased literacy (especially female literacy), better access to family planning programmes, and rising age at marriage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per the 2011 Census, India's decadal growth rate (2001-2011) further declined to about 17.7%, continuing the post-1981 trend.

 

• India's National Population Policy, 2000 aimed to further stabilise population growth through targeted socio-demographic goals.

 

NOTE

 

• 1991 (Option 1): The decline had already begun a decade earlier, in 1981, not starting from 1991.

 

• 1971 (Option 3): Growth rate was still rising or near its peak around this period, not yet declining.

 

• 1951 (Option 4): This period saw rising growth rates as India entered a phase of high birth rate and falling death rate (early demographic transition), not decline.

question: In which year Gay Lussac’s Law of Gaseous Volumes was given by Gay Lussac?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1808.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac, a French chemist, proposed the Law of Combining Volumes (Gay-Lussac's Law of Gaseous Volumes) in the year 1808. (गे-लूसाक का गैस आयतन नियम — 1808)

 

• The law states that when gases react with each other, they do so in volumes that bear a simple whole-number ratio to one another and to the volume of the product, provided all volumes are measured at the same temperature and pressure.

 

• This law was crucial in the historical development of atomic and molecular theory, later helping Amedeo Avogadro formulate his own hypothesis in 1811.

 

• Gay-Lussac is also known for his earlier Pressure-Temperature Law (Gay-Lussac's Law), which relates gas pressure and temperature at constant volume.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Avogadro's Law (1811), which states that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules, was proposed partly to explain Gay-Lussac's observations.

 

• Gay-Lussac also contributed to the discovery/isolation of boron and studies on cyanogen.

 

NOTE

 

• 1812 (Option 1): Not the correct year; the law was proposed a few years earlier, in 1808.

 

• 1800 (Option 2): Too early; Gay-Lussac had not yet formulated this law at that time.

 

• 1802 (Option 4): This year is associated with Gay-Lussac's earlier work on the pressure-temperature relationship of gases, not the law of gaseous volumes (1808).
